name: Answerline API
description:
Answerline tracks how AI assistants and search engines answer, across providers and regions. Each request comes back as structured JSON holding the engine's answer: the parsed text, its cited sources and whatever else the engine returned with them, geo-targeted to a country you choose (which countries are available depends on the engine; see [coverage](/docs/coverage)).

## Authentication

Pass your API key in the header `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. You can create keys yourself at https://dashboard.answerline.dev/keys, and each new account begins on a free tier with 500 one-time credits. A single key works for all endpoints; keys cannot currently be limited to particular scopes.

## Versioning and deprecation

The URL path carries the version. All endpoints sit under `/v1/`; no header or query parameter selects a version.

Changes inside a version only add things: new endpoints, optional request fields and response fields may be introduced at any moment. Clients have to skip response fields they don't know. Anything breaking ships under a new path (`/v2/`) and never replaces an existing version.

Deprecation is announced in the endpoint's responses themselves, not just in a changelog: the `Deprecation` header (RFC 9745) gives the date it became deprecated, `Sunset` (RFC 8594) gives the date it will stop answering, and the replacement is given by a `Link` header carrying `rel="deprecation"`. For generally available endpoints, those two dates are at least six months apart. No endpoint is currently deprecated.

## Rate limits

Each response reports the current limit state, letting a client pace itself using the response in hand: `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, plus the headers for concurrency and credits. Rate limiting uses a one-second window, so a `429` caused by it goes away almost at once; a `429` caused by the concurrency limit goes away once your running jobs complete. `Retry-After` is not set on either, and no IETF `RateLimit-*` headers are sent.

## Errors

All 4xx and 5xx responses share the `Error` envelope: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details", "timestamp" } }`. Clients should branch on `code`, a stable identifier meant for machines; `message` is meant for people reading logs.
